key_insight: Clipped decentralized SGD can achieve optimal convergence under heavy-tailed noise while preserving enough gradient magnitude information to keep consensus errors controlled.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical decentralized optimization rule for distributed ML systems that are robust to outlier gradients and scale well with more agents.
method: Apply gradient clipping at each local worker before decentralized SGD updates.
Analyze smooth non-convex objectives with bounded p-th moment noise for p in (1,2].
Use a sharp consensus-gap bound showing network effects enter only as higher-order terms, enabling linear speed-up.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical high-probability and expectation rates, plus numerical experiments that validate the convergence claims and linear speed-up.
watch_item: Clipping must be tuned carefully: too aggressive a threshold may slow progress, while the guarantees rely on the specific heavy-tailed noise and smoothness assumptions.
paper_title: Decentralized SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Optimal Convergence Rates and the Role of Gradient Clipping
